transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, the recent government export-control order has interrupted shipments of a key component used in our industrial equipment, and several counterparties have already reached out asking for our contractual position. Our principal supply agreement does contain a force-majeure provision, but we have not yet sent an external notice under that provision. Before we do, I want to walk through this cross-functional review so each of you can report your findings and recommended action. Let's start with operations — what's our current inventory situation and how long can we sustain production?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I confirmed with our plant managers this morning that exactly two of our five facilities are directly affected by the export-control order. The remaining three facilities can produce only 40% of normal output until the order is lifted. I should note that I haven't yet updated the legal incident file because operations is still reconciling its inventory report, but I wanted to get this information to the group now given the urgency of the notice decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an important insurance constraint. After reviewing our applicable supply-interruption endorsement, I confirmed that our carrier must be notified within 10 calendar days of this event. Additionally, the endorsement requires that we make no admission of liability in our customer communications. I have not yet sent the carrier notice because the claim package is still awaiting our finalized legal position on force majeure. So as we work through the force-majeure analysis today, we need to be mindful of both the 10-day carrier notification deadline and the restriction on admissions of liability in any customer-facing messages.

Samuel's insurance constraints — the 10-day carrier notification window and the no-admission-of-liability restriction — are critical guardrails for how we draft both the force-majeure notice and any customer-facing messages.
